_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with relapsed follicular B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (FL) who have received at least two prior systemic therapies, and relapsed small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) who have received at least two prior systemic therapies (accelerated approval based on ORR). The combined label also includes relapsed CLL in combination with rituximab.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Protocol 101-09, a Phase 2 study of idelalisib in subjects with indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas refractory to rituximab and alkylating agents
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, multicenter, single-arm Phase 2 trial of idelalisib 150 mg orally twice daily
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsed FL (N=72) and relapsed SLL (N=26) who had relapsed within 6 months following rituximab and an alkylating agent and had received at least 2 prior treatments
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Independent Review Committee-assessed overall response rate (ORR)
pivotal_trials.n: FL cohort N=72; SLL cohort N=26 (125 subjects enrolled overall in Protocol 101-09)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=20%): diarrhea, pyrexia, fatigue, nausea, cough, pneumonia, abdominal pain, chills, and rash. Fatal and/or serious hepatotoxicity in 14% and severe diarrhea/colitis (Grade >=3) in 14% of Zydelig-treated patients; fatal and serious pneumonitis and intestinal perforation can occur.
target_moa: Idelalisib is an inhibitor of PI3K-delta kinase, which is expressed in normal and malignant B-cells; it induces apoptosis and inhibits proliferation and B-cell receptor (BCR), CXCR4 and CXCR5 signaling involved in B-cell trafficking and homing.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for fatal and serious toxicities: hepatic (hepatotoxicity in 14%), severe diarrhea, colitis (in 14%), pneumonitis, and intestinal perforation.

rems.type: REMS consisting of a communication plan to ensure understanding of the serious risks (hepatotoxicity including fatalities, bowel perforation, colitis and pneumonitis).

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not discussed by the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee.

citations.quote: Accelerated approval was granted for FL and SLL based on overall response rate. Improvement in patient survival or disease related symptoms has not been established. Continued approval for these indications may be contingent upon verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Successful completion of either trial GS-US-313-0124 (PMR 2180-2) or GS-US-313-0125 (PMR 2180-3), randomized placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials in previously treated indolent NHL, may be adequate to convert accelerated approval to regular approval for FL and SLL.

citations.quote: Successful completion of either PMR 2180-2 or PMR 2180-3 may be adequate, after review, to convert the accelerated approval to regular approval for relapsed follicular B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (FL) in patients who have received at least two prior systemic therapies and for relapsed small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) in patients who have received at least two prior systemic therapies.

orphan_indication.text: Idelalisib has FDA Orphan Designation for several indications and is therefore exempt from PREA pediatric study requirements.

citations.quote: Idelalisib has FDA Orphan Designation for several indications (Table 5) and is therefore exempt from the Pediatric Research Equity Act pediatric study requirements.

summary.text: NDA 205858 was submitted September 11, 2013 and given standard review; it was approved under accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.500) for relapsed FL and SLL based on overall response rate, with confirmatory trials required and orphan drug designation in place.

citations.quote: NDA 205858 was submitted on September 11, 2013 for the following indication: for the treatment of patients with refractory indolent Non-Hodgkins Lymphoma.
It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.500), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.
Accelerated approval was granted for FL and SLL based on overall response rate.
